title: Savings Calculator: how it works, formula and examples
excerpt: Savings Calculator: Plan how fast your savings reach a goal. Learn how to use it, the formula behind it, a worked example and answers to common questions.
content:
The [Savings Calculator](/savings-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Plan how fast your savings reach a goal. Enter your starting balance, monthly deposit, annual interest (APY) and years and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

A savings calculator projects your balance from regular deposits and interest, helping you set realistic goals for an emergency fund, a home deposit or a holiday. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers. Related Finance tools include [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator), [Mortgage Calculator](/mortgage-calculator) and [Car Loan Calculator](/car-loan-calculator).

## How to use the Savings Calculator

Start by entering your starting balance, then entering your monthly deposit, entering your annual interest (APY) (%) and finally entering your years. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Enter your starting balance.
2. Enter your monthly deposit.
3. Enter your annual interest (apy) (%).
4. Enter your years.
5. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
6. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

Balance = P(1 + r/12)^(12t) + monthly deposit × ((1 + r/12)^(12t) − 1) ÷ (r/12).

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Savings Calculator](/savings-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. Starting with 2,000 and saving 300 a month at 4.5% grows to about 22,700 after 5 years. Try the same figures in the [Savings Calculator](/savings-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Starting balance: 2000, Monthly deposit: 300, Annual interest (APY): 4.5 %, Years: 5), the [Savings Calculator](/savings-calculator) returns Ending balance: 22,647.26, Total deposits: 20,000, Interest earned: 2,647.26. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Automate deposits on payday.
- Keep 3–6 months of expenses as an emergency fund.
- Shop around for high-yield savings accounts.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### How much should I save each month?

A popular guideline is the 50/30/20 rule — aim to save about 20% of take-home pay. You can use it as often as you like, and because nothing is uploaded, stored or tracked, there is nothing to delete afterwards.

### Is APY the same as interest rate?

APY includes the effect of compounding, so it's slightly higher than the nominal rate. Try it with your own numbers in the [Savings Calculator](/savings-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Savings Calculator use?

Balance = P(1 + r/12)^(12t) + monthly deposit × ((1 + r/12)^(12t) − 1) ÷ (r/12). You can see it in action in the [Savings Calculator](/savings-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the Savings Calculator?

Just Starting balance, Monthly deposit, Annual interest (APY) and Years. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
